issueOrPullRequest.title: build: remove bundled docs and open h3.dev from `h3 docs`
issueOrPullRequest.body:
Stops shipping the docs inside the npm package to make it smaller.

- `build.config.ts`: removed the `end()` hook that exported `./docs` into `dist/docs` with mdzilla.
- `package.json` / lockfile: removed the `mdzilla` dev dependency.
- `bin/h3.mjs`: `h3 docs [page]` now opens `https://h3.dev/<page>` with the system's open command (`open` / `xdg-open` / `cmd /c start`). If no browser can be launched, it prints the URL instead.
- `test/unit/cli.test.ts`: replaced the old tests for the bundled docs folder with a test that checks the CLI points at h3.dev.

Note: mdzilla's `--page <path>` flag is gone; use a plain page argument instead (`h3 docs /guide`).

Verified: `pnpm build` produces no `dist/docs`; the CLI test, lint and typecheck pass.

issueOrPullRequest.title: fix(body): match form content type case-insensitively in `readBody`
issueOrPullRequest.body:
`readBody()` decides whether to parse the body as url-encoded with a case-sensitive `startsWith("application/x-www-form-urlencoded")`. Media types are case-insensitive (RFC 9110, section 8.3.1: "The type and subtype tokens are case-insensitive."), so a request with a differently cased type falls through to `JSON.parse` and gets a 400:

```js
app.post("/", (event) => readBody(event));
```

```
$ curl -s localhost:3000 -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'a=1&b=2'
{"a":"1","b":"2"}
$ curl -s localhost:3000 -H 'content-type: Application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'a=1&b=2'
{"status":400,"statusText":"Bad Request","message":"Invalid JSON body"}
```

`readBody(event, { type: "formData" })` already accepts the same request, since `Request.formData()` parses the header case-insensitively, so the default path was the odd one out.

The fix lowercases the header before the check. The new test sends two differently cased form content types (one with a `charset` parameter) through the web and node matrix; without the source change both fail with `expected { status: 400, ... } to deeply equal { field: 'value', ... }`.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * URL-encoded form bodies are now parsed correctly when the `Content-Type` header uses uppercase or mixed-case letters, including with a charset parameter.

issueOrPullRequest.title: fix(response): omit HEAD body for default errors
issueOrPullRequest.body:
Resolves #1594.

Without an `onError` hook, a missing HEAD route or a handler throwing `HTTPError` returns a JSON body through the web Response API. Node's HTTP transport strips it, and a no-op `onError` hook already makes the web response body empty.

Let the generated default error response continue through the existing Response normalization path so HEAD bodies are removed consistently. The implementation changes one line; error serialization, status/statusText, error headers, cookies, and public APIs remain unchanged.

The regression matrix covers missing HEAD routes, synchronous/asynchronous HTTPError handlers, GET JSON responses, both hook configurations, preserved error headers, and hook invocation counts. Before the fix, three web HEAD cases fail and the other 17 matrix cases pass. The minimal reproduction is in #1594.

Validation on Node.js 24.21.0 / pnpm 12.3.4:

- Error handling and bundle-budget tests: 75 passed.
- Lint, typecheck, build, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Full `pnpm test`: 3055 passed, 51 skipped, one Node body-limit test timed out after 5000ms. The unmodified main at `66cfb8a` also times out in the Node body-limit suite; a lower-worker retry did not eliminate it. The full suite is therefore not green locally.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Error responses now follow consistent response processing. Missing routes and thrown HTTP errors return the expected status and error details for `GET` requests, while `HEAD` responses remain bodyless.
  * Error headers and cookies are preserved, and success-only headers are excluded from error responses.

issueOrPullRequest.title: fix(sse): preserve empty event ids
issueOrPullRequest.body:
An SSE message with `id: ""` must send an empty `id` field so an EventSource client can clear its last event ID. The current truthiness check drops that field, leaving the previous reconnection cursor in effect. The [HTML SSE specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream) defines an empty `id` value as resetting the last event ID.

Check whether the optional ID is a string so empty IDs are emitted and omitted IDs remain omitted. Wire-format regressions cover both a single message and an empty ID following a non-empty ID in a batch.

Validation on Node 24.21.0:
- Both new wire-format cases fail before the fix; all 53 SSE unit and integration tests pass after it.
- Lint, formatting, typecheck and `pnpm build` pass.
- The full unmodified test fixture run reports only the existing loopback IP expectation failure (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`); 3,037 tests pass, 51 skip after `pnpm build` (matching the CI build/test order). Applying the independent loopback test expectation locally allows the full suite to pass (3,038 passed, 51 skipped); that test-only change is excluded from this PR.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Empty event IDs are now included in formatted event stream messages, both individually and in batches. IDs continue to have newline characters removed.
* **Documentation**
  * Clarified that an empty event ID resets the client’s last event ID, while omitting the ID leaves it unchanged.
  * Added documentation explaining that event stream comments are terminated by a blank line.

issueOrPullRequest.title: fix(cors): make stateful origin regex checks repeatable
issueOrPullRequest.body:
Reusing a global or sticky RegExp in the CORS origin array makes permission depend on its `lastIndex`. The same allowed origin can alternate between accepted and rejected requests, and checking an origin mutates the caller's regex state.

For these stateful regexes, check from index zero and restore the previous index in `finally`. Ordinary regexes keep their existing path. Regression cases cover both flags, repeated accepted origins, rejected origins and preservation of a pre-existing index.

Validation on Node 24.21.0:
- Both new regression cases fail before the fix; all 52 CORS unit tests pass after it.
- Lint, formatting, typecheck and `pnpm build` pass.
- The full unmodified test fixture run reports only the existing loopback IP expectation failure (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`); 3,037 tests pass, 51 skip after `pnpm build` (matching the CI build/test order). Applying the independent loopback test expectation locally allows the full suite to pass (3,038 passed, 51 skipped); that test-only change is excluded from this PR.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed inconsistent CORS origin checks when matching rules use global or sticky regular expressions. Repeated checks now reliably allow matching origins and reject nonmatching ones, without changing the rule’s existing state.
* **Tests**

issueOrPullRequest.title: test: accept exact loopback addresses in fingerprint checks
issueOrPullRequest.body:
The Node fingerprint test fails on a dual-stack local listener when the peer address is `::ffff:127.0.0.1`. This is a valid loopback address, but the existing expectation accepts only `0.0.0.0` or `::1` (and does not anchor both alternatives).

Accept the exact loopback forms `127.0.0.1` and `::ffff:127.0.0.1` alongside the existing values, with the entire expression anchored. Arbitrary addresses and partial string matches still fail. No runtime behavior changes.

Validation on Node 24.21.0:
- The unchanged assertion reproduced one failure in `test/utils.test.ts` (197 passed).
- `pnpm test`: lint, formatting, typecheck and coverage passed; 3,036 tests passed, 51 skipped after `pnpm build` (matching the CI build/test order).

fix(static): serve .wasm as application/wasm
issueOrPullRequest.body:
`.wasm` isn't in `COMMON_MIME_TYPES`, so `serveStatic` sends it as `text/plain; charset=UTF-8` on node and with no content-type on web. `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming()` requires `application/wasm` and rejects the response otherwise.

`instantiateStreaming(await app.request("/module.wasm"))` on node 22:

```
main: TypeError: WebAssembly response has unsupported MIME type 'null'
this: ok
```

added it to the table, with a test that fails on main for web and node.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * `.wasm` files are now served with the `application/wasm` content type.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

issueOrPullRequest.title: fix(static): match file extensions case-insensitively
issueOrPullRequest.body:
`getType` looks the extension up as-is, so `/photos/IMG_0001.JPG` or `/LOGO.PNG` gets no type from `serveStatic`. on node the response then goes out as `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`, on web with no content-type at all. uppercase extensions are pretty common for camera uploads.

lowercased the extension before the lookup. the custom `getType` option still gets the extension as written.

added a test that fails on main for both web and node:

```
AssertionError: expected 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8' to be 'image/jpeg'
```


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Uppercase and mixed-case file extensions now resolve to the correct MIME type.
